static_traits.name: Chen Ming
static_traits.social_status: Having friends to talk to, but not yet sharing feelings of failure with them
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems before; has not received psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Evident self-negation, with all-or-nothing thinking, overgeneralization, and mental filtering; able to clearly express the current situation and thoughts; attitude rather negative but willing to try behavioral experiments; speech rate and cooperation not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: Because I often overcook foods I love (such as pizza and burritos), I persistently feel 'I am a failure in life,' with feelings of incompetence and self-criticism; the problem began recently when I started living alone and cooking for myself, and has gradually generalized to other areas of life.
basic_info.core_demands: After feelings of failure began to affect self-esteem and enjoyment of once-loved activities, the client hopes to relieve self-failure feelings and self-criticism through counseling.
growth_experiences: The client recently began living alone and cooking their own meals. Each time the client cooks (such as pizza or wraps), the food is often overcooked, triggering strong self-blame and feelings of incompetence; this sense of failure gradually spread from cooking to daily domains such as shopping and work, making the client believe that 'every small mistake proves I am not good enough'. At the same time, the client tried to improve cooking skills and seek others' recognition, but this did not bring relief.

special_situations.event: Cooking alone (such as pizza or burritos) and overcooking the food
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot even cook a simple meal well, it means I am a failure in life
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Gave up continuing to practice cooking, instead choosing foods that require no cooking or ordering takeout; repeatedly doubts themselves during cooking
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot even do this well; my life is a failure too

special_situations.event: Before starting to cook, recalls past failures and worries about messing up again
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I failed before, I will surely fail this time; rather than being hit again, it is better not to try
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids cooking, or only chooses extremely simple, no-cook foods to reduce risk
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will mess it up again; there is no need to try anymore

special_situations.event: Making small mistakes in daily activities such as shopping or work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Any small mistake can prove I am not good enough, I am not competent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly recalling mistakes and ignoring the parts done right, worsening self-criticism

special_situations.event: Seeking recognition or feedback from others to relieve feelings of failure but with little effect
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only with others' affirmation do I count as valuable; without external recognition, no progress counts
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly seeks recognition and reassurance from others; attributes positive feedback to chance and downplays its value
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If others do not approve of me, I am a failure

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen as competent and independent, able to handle life and matters like cooking well and gain recognition
core_conflict.fear: Fears failure leading to a collapse of self-worth, being negated and humiliated; worries that any mistake proves they are not good enough
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of failing again through self-criticism and avoiding cooking
Seeking external recognition to temporarily relieve insecurity
Tightens standards and acts cautiously to maintain fragile self-esteem

object_relations.object_representation: A picky judge (who may negate me)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to try new methods (such as behavioral experiments) or encouraged to keep practicing cooking
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understands trying as 'must succeed, otherwise it proves once again that I am incapable', and presupposes the outcome will not change (pessimistic expectation)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a negative, skeptical tone, emphasizes past failures and reasons that 'there will be no change', using negating predictions to refuse trying.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When cooking fails or small mistakes occur in daily activities and they are asked about their experience or the details
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Treats mistakes as a verdict on overall worth, believing 'I do not deserve it, I am not good enough'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses strongly self-blaming and self-deprecating statements, magnifying mistakes and ignoring positives, with a heavy and negating tone.

manifestations: Generalizes a cooking failure into 'I have failed in life'
Decreased enjoyment of activities (cooking, shopping)
Positive events are covered by feelings of failure, difficulty remembering moments done well
outcomes: Avoids trying, reduces participation in life
Increased anxiety and sense of frustration

manifestations: Recently living alone and handling daily affairs alone
Although there are friends to talk to, has not shared one's failures and feelings
outcomes: Aggravating doubt about and anxiety over one's self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths.
manifestations: Judging oneself by the rigid standard 'should be able to do simple things well'
Internalizing 'cooking must succeed' as a yardstick for self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual turns the energy originally directed outward onto the self, restraining or giving up outward expression and action.
manifestations: After cooking failure, turning anger and disappointment into self-blame and self-deprecation
Chooses to avoid trying cooking again and orders takeout to suppress discomfort

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection with excessive self-restriction and reproach, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Excessive worry and repeated self-doubt before cooking
Views small mistakes as overall incompetence; harsh self-judgment

positive_force: Possesses some self-observation ability, able to describe thoughts and emotions before, during, and after cooking
Willing to try new methods (such as choosing simple recipes, preparing ingredients in advance)
Has some social support resources (friends to talk with)
Able to formulate concrete small-step plans (choosing simple recipes, preparing in advance)
negative_force: Self-negation and low self-esteem; often defines self-worth by mistakes
All-or-nothing thinking and overgeneralization, easily generalizing a single failure to overall failure
Mental filtering and disqualifying the positive; a sense of failure overshadows positive experiences
Dependence on external approval; insufficient internal self-affirmation
Avoiding attempts to reduce anxiety in the short term, reinforcing the 'incompetence' self-schema in the long term

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids cooking and skill-based activities, instead ordering takeout or choosing no-cook foods
antecedent: High anxiety and self-doubt before starting to cook
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing of failure and predicting inevitable future failure (all-or-nothing rules, fortune telling), in order to protect fragile self-esteem
target_behavior.function: Escapes failure and anxiety, gaining short-term emotional relief
target_behavior.consequence: Deepens the self-perception of 'I can't do it', living costs increase, and enjoyment and self-efficacy decline further

target_behavior.behavior: Strong self-deprecation and self-criticism (such as 'I am worthless')
antecedent: Failing at cooking or making small mistakes at shopping or work
When reviewing daily performance, focusing only on mistakes
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized negative core belief (I am not good enough), using mistakes as global evidence supporting that belief
target_behavior.function: Uses self-blame as a means of self-control and preventing further attempts, avoiding facing again the shame brought by failure
target_behavior.consequence: Damaged self-esteem, low mood and increased avoidance, decreased life participation

target_behavior.behavior: High anxiety and distraction during cooking, leading to frequently overcooking the food
antecedent: Worrying about failing again when cooking alone
Repeated second-guessing and self-doubt during cooking
target_behavior.core_reason: High sensitivity to mistakes and excessive monitoring weaken focus and execution, forming a negative feedback loop
target_behavior.function: Trying to gain a sense of control through excessive monitoring in the present (but it backfires)
target_behavior.consequence: Persistently poor cooking results further reinforce feelings of failure and avoidance behavior
